Which capability class serves that?

options.A: The existing image model, generating a run of stills that the induction module plays one after another.
options.B: The multimodal deployment that reads campus photographs, prompted to produce the demonstration clip.
options.C: A video generation model, which is the capability class for moving visual output made from a description.
options.D: A phone recording of a walk along the route, with a model writing captions over the resulting footage.

rationale.correct: Video generation models are taught as their own capability alongside image generation, so a requirement for moving visual output is served by a different model class from the one that produces stills. Create new visual outputs by using generative models covers both, and the safety office asked for movement worked up from a description.

distractors.A: A run of stills played in sequence is the stills capability stretched past what it produces, and the module still has no moving demonstration.
distractors.B: The deployment that reads campus photographs reports on images that exist. Prompting it for a clip asks an analysis capability to generate one.
distractors.D: Filming the route is what the safety office ruled out, and captioning footage describes a video without producing one.

questions.question: A paper mill is specifying a maintenance app with two visual requirements: judge from an operator's photograph whether a reel wrap fault is a crease or a tear, and produce an illustrative picture of a correctly wrapped reel for the printed guide. A developer proposes one visual model for the whole app. Which assessment is correct?

options.A: The two requirements travel in opposite directions, so the app needs one model class to read images and another to produce them.
options.B: One multimodal deployment covers both requirements, as reading an image and producing a new one are the same visual capability at heart.
options.C: The app should generate a picture of each fault type and compare the operator's photograph against them.
options.D: The guide illustration should be made by cropping the clearest wrapped-reel photograph in the mill's archive.

rationale.correct: Analyzing images and generating them sit in the same area of computer vision work but are opposite directions of travel, so a solution that needs both needs two model classes and not one that does everything visual. Judging a photographed fault is analysis; the guide illustration is what Create new visual outputs by using generative models describes.

distractors.B: Reading and producing images are separate capability classes. Treating them as one leaves the app specified against a model that cannot do half of its job.
distractors.C: Generating a reference picture per fault type and comparing against it adds a production step and a comparison step to work a single analysis call already does.
distractors.D: A cropped archive photograph is a real illustration of a real reel. It is retrieval from what exists, which is the direction the guide requirement does not need.

keywords: lightweight application that includes vision capabilities
questions.question: An offshore wind maintenance operator has technicians photograph blade leading edges at every visit. A proof of concept sends a photograph to a deployed multimodal model and gets back a well-written paragraph about the erosion visible in it. Six weeks on, the work order system still receives nothing from the proof of concept. What is the application missing?

options.A: A larger multimodal deployment, so that the paragraphs are detailed enough for planners to rely on.
options.B: A planner who reads each paragraph and types the erosion severity into the work order system.
options.C: A store holding each paragraph with its photograph, ready for review at the next maintenance window.
options.D: A prompt stating the judgment the work order needs, and code turning the answer into a work order value.

rationale.correct: A lightweight application that includes vision capabilities carries the work end to end: it gets the image in, sends it with a prompt that states what is wanted, and turns the answer into something the business process can act on. The proof of concept stops at the paragraph, so the missing parts are the stated judgment and the step that lands it in the work order system.

distractors.A: A larger deployment writes a better paragraph. Nothing about paragraph quality moves a value into the work order system.
distractors.B: A planner retyping severity makes the operator's own staff the integration, and it scales with the number of photographs rather than with the fleet.
distractors.C: Storing paragraphs beside photographs preserves the output for later. The work order still waits, now with a tidy archive behind it.

questions.question: A construction site's gate camera has to do two jobs as each delivery arrives: capture the permit number printed on the windscreen docket, and count the pallets stacked on the flatbed. A trial that asked for one description of the gate scene returned a fluent paragraph carrying neither the permit number nor a count. Select TWO tasks the vision pipeline needs.

options.A: A caption of the windscreen area as each delivery arrives at the gate.
options.B: Character reading over the windscreen docket, so the permit number arrives as text.
options.C: Classification of each arriving flatbed as a compliant or a non-compliant delivery.
options.D: Located instances of each pallet on the flatbed, so the pallets can be counted.
options.E: Character reading over the windscreen docket for the permit number and the pallet count together.

rationale.correct: One visual requirement often needs more than one distinct visual task in the same pipeline: describing a scene, locating instances in it and reading the characters on it are separate asks that a single call does not cover. Computer vision tasks and techniques split this gate into reading the docket and locating each pallet, which is why a lightweight application that includes vision capabilities here makes two calls and not one.

distractors.A: A caption of the windscreen area describes in prose what is displayed there. The permit number has to arrive as a value the gate log can hold, and a description of the docket is not one.
distractors.C: A compliant or non-compliant verdict for the whole vehicle is a single label over the whole image. It answers neither of the gate's two questions: the permit number is still unread and the pallets are still uncounted.
distractors.E: The docket is the delivery's paperwork. Reading a count off it reports what was loaded on paper, while the gate's second job is counting the pallets that actually arrived on the flatbed.

distractors.C: The playground is an interactive surface for a person. Pasting notes into it keeps every delivery dependent on someone doing the copying.

questions.question: An agricultural equipment dealership handles warranty claims that arrive as a mix: a typed email from the farm, a scanned service sheet, a photograph of the failed component, and a voicemail from the field technician. A draft architecture proposes four separate services, one per kind of content. Which assessment is correct?

rationale.correct: One tool spans all four content types, so a solution facing mixed content does not need a different service per modality — that unifying claim is what the four parallel extraction tasks state together. Content Understanding takes the email, the scanned sheet, the photograph and the voicemail on the same path and returns the claim's values from each.

distractors.B: A product per content type is how the work used to be split. It multiplies what the dealership integrates and pays for to reach the same values.
distractors.C: Converting everything into documents inserts a conversion stage in front of a tool that already accepts the original content types.
distractors.D: Automating the easy half and routing the rest to staff leaves the two content types that arrive from the field as manual work forever.

questions.question: A fire-safety compliance contractor has extraction running over inspection certificates, and a spot check confirms the values it returns are accurate. questions.question: An aerial survey mapping company keeps flight logs, landowner consent letters, calibration certificates and invoices together in one archive. The team configured extraction for flight logs and ran the whole archive through it. Flight logs came back well; consent letters came back empty or with values taken from the wrong part of the page. What should the design do differently?

options.A: Raise the confidence threshold on the extraction so that the poor results are discarded automatically.
options.B: Sort the archive by content type first, then run the extraction configured for each type against its own group.
options.C: Configure one extraction that covers every field found across all four kinds of document in the archive.
options.D: Run each configuration over the whole archive in turn and keep whichever run returns the most fields.

rationale.correct: A mixed archive is sorted by content type before any type-specific extraction runs, because extraction configured for one kind of document produces nothing useful when it is handed another kind. Classifying first is what gives Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools a group whose Field extraction and mapping configuration actually matches the pages in it.

distractors.A: A higher threshold hides the bad results instead of producing good ones, and the consent letters end up excluded rather than extracted.
distractors.C: One configuration covering every field across four document kinds asks each page to be matched against fields it never contains, which is the fault repeated at greater scale.
distractors.D: Running every configuration over everything and keeping the fullest result trades a sorting step for repeated processing and a guess about which run was right.
